title: Hezekiah
lead: King of Judah about 715–686 BC, son of Ahaz and father of Manasseh. Kings praises him above all kings of Judah for his trust in the LORD; his reign saw the fall of Samaria, Sennacherib's invasion of 701 BC and Jerusalem's escape, his illness and recovery, and the building of the Siloam tunnel.

sections.b: Hezekiah's story is told three times: in 2 Kings 18–20, in Isaiah 36–39 (nearly word for word, with Hezekiah's song of thanks in Isaiah 38:9–20), and in 2 Chronicles 29–32, which adds his temple cleansing and a great Passover open to the north. Proverbs 25:1 says "the men of Hezekiah" copied out proverbs of Solomon. Jeremiah 26:18–19 remembers that he listened to Micah's warning and so turned God's judgment away. Matthew 1:9–10 names him among Jesus' ancestors.
